newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Banking sector boosts Moroccan bourse slightly.
newsitem.headline: Banking sector boosts Moroccan bourse slightly.

text.p: The banking sector drove the Casablanca stock exchange slightly up on Thursday compared with the previous session, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 435.10 points, up 0.03 percent over the previous session.

"The market is returning slowly to an upward trend after three days of fluctuation...But the stocks closing price remains flat and are expected to stay nearly at the same level in the next few weeks," an analyst at Upline Securities said.

Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the largest capitalisation firm, gained three dirhams to close at 690 dirhams. Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie closed at 318 dirhams, up three dirhams over the previous session.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the blue chips and competitive banks, was traded at 400 dirhams, unchanged.
Credit Immobilier et Hotelier was also stable at 188 dirhams. The bank is expected to be privatised soon, stockbrokers said.
Samir oil refinery, Morocco's main refinery was unchanged at 250 dirhams.
The authorities may delay the second part of its privatisation of Samir due to lack of interesting offers, officials said.
It was earlier expected to be offered between November and December this year.
An official at the privatisation ministry said the initial plan of set up Samir's hard core may take place some time in 1997. He declined to give details.
Traded volume on the official market was 28.7 million dirhams against 30.2 million on Wednesday. ($1= 8.6 dirhams)
